meta.title: Nephrology Literature Update
meta.query: Clinical nephrology — RCTs, systematic reviews & meta-analyses (humans, English)
meta.source: PubMed (NLM) abstracts; summaries authored by Google NotebookLM. Each entry links to its PubMed record and DOI.
meta.note: Summaries and PICO are NotebookLM analyses of the source abstracts; criteria marked “not specified” were not stated.
meta.appraisal_source: Professor critical appraisal (clinical bottom-line, relevance, caveat).

articles.authors: Pei X, Gao H, Zhang L
articles.title: Diagnostic and prognostic value of fibroblast growth factor 23 in acute kidney injury: systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: This meta-analysis of 23 studies showed circulating FGF23 has a pooled sensitivity of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.73-0.86), specificity of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.75-0.89), and SROC AUC of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.81-0.92) for AKI diagnosis. For AKI mortality, the pooled sensitivity was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.69-0.84), specificity was 0.76 (95% CI: 0.70-0.82), and SROC AUC was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.70-0.83). iFGF23 demonstrated higher diagnostic accuracy than cFGF23, with an SROC AUC of 0.91 versus 0.81.

pico.population: Patients at risk for acute kidney injury (AKI) or AKI-related mortality
pico.intervention: Measurement of circulating intact FGF23 (iFGF23) or C-terminal FGF23 (cFGF23)
pico.comparison: No FGF23 measurement or reference standards
pico.outcome: Diagnostic and prognostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, PLR/NLR, DOR, SROC AUC) and AKI mortality

inclusion: Studies evaluating circulating intact FGF23 (iFGF23) or C-terminal FGF23 (cFGF23) in the context of AKI

appraisal.bottom_line: Circulating FGF23 exhibits moderate-to-high diagnostic performance and moderate prognostic utility for mortality in AKI.
appraisal.relevance: It has potential utility as a complementary biomarker for risk stratification in acute clinical settings.
appraisal.caveat: Clinical interpretation is limited by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 67% for diagnosis; I² = 86.2% for sensitivity and 80.4% for specificity in mortality prediction).

articles.authors: Thomas SM, Anilkumar AS, Veerabathiran R
articles.title: Protective association of the ELMO1 rs741301 variant against diabetes mellitus and diabetic nephropathy: a systematic meta-analysis of case-control studies.
articles.summary: This meta-analysis of 9 case-control studies involving 880 individuals with DM and 1,008 with DN showed a significant protective association between the ELMO1 rs741301 polymorphism and DN under the allelic model (OR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.67-0.88), recessive model (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.61-0.90), and dominant model (OR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.53-0.88). No statistically significant association was observed under the over-dominant model.

pico.comparison: Absence of ELMO1 rs741301 polymorphism / alternative genotypes

inclusion: Case-control studies published between 2014 and 2024 investigating the association between ELMO1 rs741301 and DN among individuals with DM according to predefined inclusion criteria

appraisal.bottom_line: The ELMO1 rs741301 polymorphism is associated with a significantly reduced susceptibility to DN among individuals with diabetes.
appraisal.relevance: Provides solid evidence of a genetic contribution of ELMO1 to DN susceptibility, highlighting potential targets for understanding diabetic complications.
appraisal.caveat: Further well-designed studies in diverse populations are necessary to validate and generalize this genetic association.

articles.authors: Ma J, Liu B, Pang J, Wang P, Li Y et al.
articles.title: Efficacy and safety of ferric citrate tablets in Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia undergoing maintenance hemodialysis: a multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, phase III trial.
articles.summary: In this Phase III trial of 239 maintenance hemodialysis patients, the mean change in serum phosphorus was -0.70 ± 0.50 mmol/L with ferric citrate versus -0.61 ± 0.59 mmol/L with sevelamer carbonate, confirming non-inferiority (LS mean difference: -0.09 mmol/L, 95% CI: -0.24 to 0.05 mmol/L, within the 0.32 mmol/L margin). No significant inter-group difference was found in the percentage of patients achieving target phosphorus levels (49.09% vs. 48.28%, p = 0.902). Ferric citrate also significantly improved iron-related parameters and hemoglobin.

pico.population: Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia undergoing maintenance hemodialysis
pico.outcome: Change in serum phosphorus levels from baseline to week 12 (primary); changes in serum calcium, intact PTH, safety, iron-related parameters, and hemoglobin levels (secondary)

inclusion: Chinese patients with hyperphosphatemia on maintenance hemodialysis

appraisal.bottom_line: Ferric citrate tablets are non-inferior to sevelamer carbonate in reducing serum phosphorus levels in hyperphosphatemia patients on maintenance hemodialysis.
appraisal.relevance: Offers a highly valuable dual therapeutic benefit by managing hyperphosphatemia while simultaneously treating iron-deficiency anemia in dialysis patients.
appraisal.caveat: The trial was open-label, limited to 12 weeks, and conducted strictly in a Chinese patient population.

articles.authors: Zhang Q, Gong T, Ye Y
articles.title: The Impact of Educational or Behavioural Interventions on Fatigue in Adults Receiving Haemodialysis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: This meta-analysis of 30 studies showed that self-management education significantly reduced fatigue in hemodialysis patients (SMD = 0.98, 95% CI: [0.69, 1.28], p < 0.001; moderate certainty). Exercise training also demonstrated a significant benefit (SMD = 0.82, 95% CI: [0.44, 1.20], p < 0.001; low certainty). However, cognitive behavioral therapy did not yield a statistically significant effect (SMD = 1.45, 95% CI: [-0.46, 3.37], p = 0.137; very low certainty).

pico.intervention: Self-management education, exercise training, or cognitive behavioural therapy
pico.outcome: Fatigue (standardised mean differences based on change scores)

inclusion: Randomised controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies investigating the effectiveness of educational or behavioral interventions on fatigue in hemodialysis patients

appraisal.bottom_line: Self-management education and exercise training significantly reduce fatigue in adult hemodialysis patients, while cognitive behavioral therapy's clinical efficacy remains unproven.
appraisal.relevance: Self-management education should be considered for routine clinical integration, with exercise training serving as an adjunctive fatigue-management strategy.
appraisal.caveat: Evidence certainty was low for exercise and very low for CBT, highlighting the clear need for further high-quality trials.

articles.authors: Wang D, Wang Z, Wang D, Lei W, Lu Y et al.
articles.title: Effects of flurbiprofen axetil on postoperative renal function in patients undergoing percutaneous nephrolithotomy: A prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical study.
articles.summary: In this randomized trial of 120 patients undergoing percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL), the postoperative administration of 100 mg flurbiprofen axetil did not significantly reduce clinical AKI incidence compared to saline control (1 case vs. 5 cases, p = 0.207). However, NGAL levels at 6 hours postoperatively were significantly lower in the flurbiprofen group compared to the control group (184.84 ± 43.14 vs. 216.35 ± 63.39, p = 0.002). There were no significant differences in serum creatinine, NGAL, or cystatin C at any other postoperative time points.

pico.population: Patients undergoing percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) under general anesthesia
pico.intervention: Postoperative intravenous administration of 100 mg of flurbiprofen axetil
pico.comparison: Postoperative intravenous administration of 10 ml of normal saline
pico.outcome: Incidence of perioperative AKI, and postoperative levels of serum creatinine, glomerular filtration rate (GFR), cystatin C, and NGAL

inclusion: Patients undergoing PCNL under general anesthesia between February and July 2025

appraisal.bottom_line: Postoperative flurbiprofen axetil (100 mg) significantly reduces NGAL levels at 6 hours post-PCNL, but does not significantly reduce clinical AKI rates.
appraisal.relevance: Provides early biochemical evidence suggesting a potential acute protective effect on renal function, challenging historical concerns about NSAID use post-PCNL.
appraisal.caveat: The study was small (120 completed patients) and likely underpowered to detect significant differences in clinical AKI incidence (p = 0.207).

articles.authors: Hsu JW, Wang HP, Chiang TI
articles.title: Role of fibroblast growth factor 23 in predicting CKD progression and prognosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: This meta-analysis of 12 prospective cohort studies (21,042 pre-dialysis CKD patients) showed that elevated FGF-23 levels were associated with lower eGFR (mean difference: 17.83 mL/min/1.73m²). In mild-moderate CKD, each 10 RU/mL increase in FGF-23 conferred a 1.7% higher risk of kidney failure (HR = 1.01, 95% CI: [1.01-1.02]), while in advanced CKD, the highest vs. lowest FGF-23 quartile was associated with a 2.32-fold increased risk of kidney failure (95% CI: [1.80-2.98]). High FGF-23 was associated with increased risk of cardiovascular events (HR = 1.72, 95% CI: [1.34-2.20]), heart failure (HR = 2.14, 95% CI: [1.53-3.00]), and all-cause mortality (HR = 1.61, 95% CI: [1.40-1.87]).

pico.population: Pre-dialysis adult patients with CKD stages 1-5
pico.comparison: Lower circulating FGF-23 levels or lowest quartile
pico.outcome: Kidney function decline, progression to kidney failure, cardiovascular events, heart failure, and all-cause mortality

inclusion: Prospective cohort studies enrolling pre-dialysis adult patients with CKD stages 1-5

appraisal.bottom_line: FGF-23 is a highly significant prognostic biomarker that independently predicts CKD progression, cardiovascular events, heart failure, and all-cause mortality.
appraisal.relevance: Measuring FGF-23 in clinical practice could allow for earlier risk stratification and more targeted clinical interventions in the pre-dialysis CKD population.
appraisal.caveat: The meta-analysis combines studies with potentially heterogeneous clinical protocols, follow-up durations, and biomarker assay definitions.

articles.authors: Vidanapathirana M, Wijayaratne D, Ariadurai J, Jayasinghe S
articles.title: Gender disparity in access to care across the continuum of chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.
articles.summary: This systematic review of 35 studies demonstrated systematic sex and gender-based inequities disadvantaging women across the entire CKD continuum. Women had lower odds of receiving a CKD diagnosis, referral, frequent GFR monitoring, or guideline-recommended medications. Among prevalent dialysis patients, women comprised only 38-41% of the cohort and initiated dialysis at lower GFRs (8.1-10.1 vs. 10.6 mL/min/1.73 m² in men). Women were also less likely to initiate hemodialysis with an AVF, transition to an AVF, or receive evaluation, discussion, waitlisting, or execution of kidney transplantation.

pico.population: Patients across the continuum of chronic kidney disease (CKD)
pico.outcome: Access to diagnostic, monitoring, guideline-directed therapy, vascular access, dialysis, and transplantation services

inclusion: Publications from 2000 to July 2026 addressing gender-based disparities across sequential steps of CKD care

appraisal.bottom_line: Systemic and socioeconomic gender-based inequities systematically disadvantage women across every sequential step of the CKD care continuum.
appraisal.relevance: Underscores a critical clinical and policy need to integrate gender-equity measures into the management guidelines and health delivery systems for CKD.
appraisal.caveat: The individual studies are observational (assessed with ROBINS-E), and local structural barriers will vary across different global regions.

articles.authors: Jia M, Wu Q, Zou J, Jin D
articles.title: A young male with kidney damage from genetic mitochondrial disease: case report and literature review.
articles.summary: This case report presents a 17-year-old male with progressive hearing loss and proteinuria (0.85 g/24h) who was found to have FSGS on biopsy (showing swollen podocytes and dysmorphic mitochondria) secondary to a mitochondrial m.3243 A > G mutation in the MT-TL1 gene, which was also present in his mother. Following mitochondrial energy support and uric acid/creatinine lowering therapies, the patient's renal function remained stable over a 23-month follow-up.

pico.population: A 17-year-old male with proteinuria, renal dysfunction (serum creatinine 2.1 mg/dl), lower extremity weakness, and progressive hearing loss
pico.intervention: Treatments to improve mitochondrial energy synthesis, reduce creatinine production, promote creatinine excretion, and lower uric acid levels
pico.outcome: Stabilization of renal function, creatinine levels, proteinuria, and uric acid levels over 23 months of follow-up

inclusion: A patient presenting with kidney damage secondary to genetic mitochondrial disease and associated FSGS

appraisal.bottom_line: The mitochondrial m.3243 A > G mutation in the MT-TL1 gene can present as an ear-kidney syndrome mimicking Alport syndrome, with FSGS pathology that may stabilize with mitochondrial energy support.
appraisal.relevance: Reminds nephrologists to take a detailed family history and suspect mitochondrial genetic diseases in patients presenting with concurrent hearing loss and glomerular pathology.
appraisal.caveat: The findings are based on a single patient case report and review, meaning larger clinical trials are necessary to prove therapeutic efficacy.

articles.authors: Adar A, Kaufman-Shriqui V, Boaz M
articles.title: Nutrition Supplements and Serum Albumin in Hemodialysis: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.summary: This meta-analysis of 8 randomized clinical trials involving 382 adult hemodialysis patients demonstrated that oral nutrition supplements (ONS) or intradialytic parenteral nutrition (IDPN) significantly increased serum albumin levels compared with controls. The pooled standardized mean difference (SMD) in serum albumin was 0.372 g/dL (95% CI: 0.103-0.641, P = 0.007). Results were highly robust across both random- and fixed-effects models, with no evidence of publication bias.

pico.intervention: Oral nutrition supplements (ONS) and/or intradialytic parenteral nutrition (IDPN)

inclusion: Randomized clinical trials published or registered from 2019 to 2024 evaluating ONS or IDPN on serum albumin in hemodialysis patients, with a Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) score of 9 or greater
exclusion: Studies scoring less than 9 on the CASP checklist

appraisal.bottom_line: ONS and IDPN significantly improve serum albumin levels in maintenance hemodialysis patients, helping to mitigate the risk of malnutrition.
appraisal.relevance: Directly supports the clinical use of oral nutrition supplements and/or IDPN in hemodialysis patients with evidence of protein-energy wasting.
appraisal.caveat: The analysis is based on a relatively small cumulative patient cohort (N = 382) across only 8 included trials.

articles.authors: Pourrezagholi F, Amini H, Omid Moradi, Mahdavi B, Nadiri Niri A et al.
articles.title: Effect of Melatonin Supplementation on Glycemic and Lipid Profiles in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Clinical Trial.
articles.summary: In this randomized trial of 84 kidney transplant recipients (42 per group), 3 months of 6 mg/day melatonin significantly decreased fasting blood sugar (FBS) by a median of 6.5 mg/dL (p < 0.001) and HbA1c by 0.25 units (p < 0.001) within the treatment group. The adjusted between-group effect favored melatonin for HbA1c (β = -0.30%, 95% CI: -0.59 to -0.01%, P < 0.001) but not for FBS (β = -2.61 mg/dL, 95% CI: -17.93 to 12.71 mg/dL, P = 0.283). Melatonin also significantly lowered triglycerides (adjusted β = -23.77 mg/dL, 95% CI: -45.50 to -2.04 mg/dL, P = 0.032), with no impact on blood pressure or renal function.

pico.population: Adult kidney transplant recipients (at least 6 months post-transplant)
pico.intervention: Melatonin supplementation at 6 mg/day for 3 months
pico.outcome: Changes in fasting blood sugar (FBS) and HbA1c levels (primary); blood pressure, lipid profile parameters, and renal function (secondary)

inclusion: Adult kidney transplant recipients who are at least 6 months post-transplantation

appraisal.bottom_line: Three months of melatonin supplementation modestly improves HbA1c and reduces serum triglycerides in kidney transplant recipients, with no adverse impact on graft function or blood pressure.
appraisal.relevance: Melatonin may serve as a safe and low-cost adjunctive therapy to manage metabolic dysregulation and cardiovascular risk post-transplant.
appraisal.caveat: The study is limited by its short duration (3 months) and small sample size (42 patients analyzed per arm).

articles.authors: Shadravan S, Khezri R, Zarei Venovel M, Mahami-Oskouei M, Hooman N
articles.title: Impact of Dapagliflozin on Kidney Function Decline in Chronic Kidney Disease Patients: A Systematic Review.
articles.summary: This systematic review of 15 trials concerning dapagliflozin in CKD patients excluded 11 overlapping publications of the DAPA-CKD trial, leaving 4 unique trials for narrative synthesis. The mean difference in eGFR decline across these studies was highly variable, ranging from -6.60 to +0.93 mL/min/1.73m², with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 93.7%) preventing meta-analysis. Despite this heterogeneity in eGFR trajectories, evidence from the parent DAPA-CKD trial suggests a reduction in the risk of adverse clinical renal outcomes.

pico.outcome: eGFR decline, CKD progression, and composite clinical renal outcomes

inclusion: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) concerning dapagliflozin in CKD patients searched up to January 10, 2025
exclusion: Overlapping publications or populations derived from the same parent trials (specifically, 11 secondary analyses of the DAPA-CKD parent trial)

appraisal.bottom_line: Dapagliflozin therapy confers renal protective benefits and is clinically safe, although its quantitative effect on eGFR decline trajectories is highly variable across different studies.
appraisal.relevance: Supports SGLT2 inhibitor therapy to prevent adverse renal outcomes, highlighting the need to look beyond surrogate eGFR slopes in clinical trials.
appraisal.caveat: Extreme heterogeneity (I² = 93.7%) and a very limited number of independent, non-overlapping trials restrict the ability to perform a quantitative meta-analysis.

articles.authors: Liu PY, Shih CK, Hsieh MH, Lin CC, Liu CY et al.
articles.title: Cardiovascular outcome of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists vs dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor on end-stage kidney disease patients with heart failure: an emulated target trial in patients with diabetes.
articles.summary: This target trial emulation in diabetic ESKD patients on dialysis with heart failure showed that initiation of GLP-1RAs significantly reduced the primary composite risk of ischemic events and HF exacerbations compared to DPP-4is (31.7% vs. 41.4%; HR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.64-0.82, p < 0.0001). Use of GLP-1RAs was also associated with concordant reductions in ischemic events (HR = 0.74), HF exacerbations (HR = 0.76), all-cause mortality (HR = 0.68), and a death-inclusive composite (HR = 0.72). Results were corroborated in a dialysis-dependence-coded HF subset (HR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.60-0.85).

pico.population: Diabetic end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) patients with heart failure (HF) undergoing maintenance dialysis
pico.intervention: Initiation of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs)
pico.outcome: Ischemic cardiovascular events plus HF exacerbations (primary composite); individual ischemic events, HF exacerbations, all-cause mortality, and death-inclusive composite outcomes

inclusion: Diabetic patients with ESKD and HF on maintenance dialysis, including a primary ESKD-HF cohort and a confirmatory dialysis-dependence-coded HF subset

appraisal.bottom_line: GLP-1RAs significantly improve composite cardiovascular events, heart failure exacerbations, and all-cause mortality compared to DPP-4is in diabetic patients with ESKD and heart failure on dialysis.
appraisal.relevance: Provides powerful real-world evidence for cardioprotection in a high-risk, dialysis-dependent patient cohort that is typically excluded from major randomized clinical trials.
appraisal.caveat: As an emulated target trial based on electronic health record data, prospective randomized clinical trials are still needed for definitive validation.
